title: Removing the last entry of a mapping, then replacing the literal scalar before it, ends as a fresh parse of the first step would
notes: `key1` is a literal scalar with content indentation 5 (production 170). `key2: v` follows it, and after `key2` comes a line of six spaces. Once `key2` is removed, that line would directly follow the literal's text, and there a line of six spaces is text of the scalar, not part of its trailer (production 166 with 167, l-strip-empty, takes only lines of at most 5 spaces): left as it is, it would change `key1` from `t` and a line break to `t`, a line break, a space and a line break. The removal must therefore take the line or shorten it. The kit takes it with the entry (docs/edit-semantics.md, Kit conventions, a whitespace-only line after a removed last entry); keeping it as an empty line would read back the same, so this is a convention. The second operation replaces `key1` with `a b`, which has no final line break, so the literal takes the strip header `|-` and keeps the old content indentation (docs/edit-semantics.md: 'Indentation of a rewritten block scalar reuses the old content's indentation'), and `after: 1` follows with nothing between. A library whose in-place state after the removal differs from a fresh parse of its own output edits the wrong bytes in the second step. The tag `convention` marks the removal of the line and the reused indentation.

provenance.reference: A patch engine whose in-place state after removing the last entry of a block mapping, with a whitespace-only line behind it that the literal scalar before it takes over, differed from a fresh parse of its own output, so the next operation edited the wrong bytes.
